**Finding: T4C — Compliant (no redline proposed).**

- **Customer convenience right present.** § 12.2(a)(i) (p0488) lets Sanofi terminate for convenience either in its entirety or on a country-by-country / Product-by-Product basis — the analogue of terminating the Agreement or an individual order.
- **No Vendor convenience right.** RevMed's termination rights are all conditional/for-cause: material breach with cure (12.2(b)), insolvency (12.2(c)), Competing Product with a cure-and-election mechanic (12.2(d)), and cessation of [***] after notice, meeting and cure (12.2(e)). This satisfies the preferred element and exceeds the fallback's tolerance for an end-of-term Vendor convenience right.
- **No early-termination fee.** The 12.3(c) consequences are licence reversion, sell-off and transition assistance; RevMed pays *us* royalties on Termination Products.
- **Noted, not flagged:** the 12.2(a)(i) notice periods are redacted ([***]) and should be confirmed against the unredacted version; and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, a preferred-only sub-element with no application to this milestone/profit-share payment structure.
